title: Algorithm Termination Conjecture
statement_text: The authors' iterative algorithm for computing regular pentagon contact representations (solve the linear system associated with the current five color forest; if the solution has negative variables, change the five color forest along the directed cycles separating negative from non-negative variables and restart) terminates with a non-negative solution for every graph $G$ which is an inner triangulation of a $5$-gon, and for every initial five color forest $F$ of $G$.
context_text: An inner triangulation of a $5$-gon is a simple plane graph whose outer face is a 5-cycle $a_1,\dots,a_5$ (clockwise), whose inner faces are triangles, and with no edges among $a_1,\dots,a_5$ other than the outer cycle. A regular pentagon contact representation of $G$ represents each inner vertex by a regular pentagon with a horizontal side at the bottom (so all pentagons are homothetic) and the outer vertices $a_1,\dots,a_5$ by the five sides $s_1,\dots,s_5$ of a large pentagon with all angles $3\pi/5$ ($s_1$ horizontal at the top), with pairwise interior-disjoint shapes such that two shapes touch exactly when the vertices are adjacent. Its existence for every such $G$ follows from Schramm's Convex Packing (Monster Packing) Theorem. A five color forest of $G$ is an orientation and colouring of the inner edges with colours $1,\dots,5$ (mod 5) such that (F1) every edge at $a_i$ is oriented towards $a_i$ and has colour $i$; (F2) at every inner vertex $v$ the incoming edges form five possibly empty blocks $B_1,\dots,B_5$ of colours $1,\dots,5$ in clockwise order, $v$ has at most one outgoing edge of each colour $i$, located between $B_{i+2}$ and $B_{i-2}$; (F3) for each $i$, $B_i$ is nonempty or $v$ has an outgoing edge of colour $i-2$ or $i+2$. Every regular pentagon contact representation induces a five color forest; five color forests are relatives of Schnyder woods, are in bijection with certain $\alpha_5$-orientations and form a distributive lattice. The algorithm starts from any five color forest $F$, builds a linear system $A_F\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{e}_1$ whose unknowns are side lengths of the skeleton of the would-be representation; a non-negative solution gives the representation, and otherwise the authors prove the negative and non-negative variables are separated by a nonempty disjoint union of directed cycles of the $\alpha_5$-orientation, which is used to change $F$. They cannot prove progress, but two implementations always succeeded in experiments; analogous algorithms for homothetic triangles and squares also lack termination proofs. A proof would give an existence proof independent of Schramm's theorem and exact coordinates; with a polynomial bound on the number of iterations, a strongly polynomial algorithm over $\mathbb{Q}[\sqrt5]$.
